izzyondroid:com.bojko108.mobiletileserve.name: Mobile Tile Server
izzyondroid:com.bojko108.mobiletileserve.summary: HTTP Server for your local Map Tiles
izzyondroid:com.bojko108.mobiletileserve.description:
Mobile Tile Server can be used as a HTTP server, serving Map Tiles from the device storage. When the server is running you can access the tiles from different mapping applications.
 The application provides four main options:
 Access of local Map Tiles
 Access of local MBTiles files
 Redirect to a Tile Server with QuadKey Tile schema
 Access static files
 Access to local Map Tiles 
 Local Map Tiles can be accessed on address: http://localhost:PORT/tiles – where PORT is set in application settings. In settings, you must specify a directory, where the files are stored. This directory is used as a root for the server. All files in that directory (including subdirectories) will be accessible from the server.
 Example: If you have map tiles stored in /storage/emulated/0/MobileTileServer/tiles/Plovdiv/{z}_{x}_{y}.png , you can set the root directory to: /storage/emulated/0/MobileTileServer . Then in order to access this map just start the service and navigate to: http://localhost:PORT/tiles/Plovdiv/{z}_{x}_{y}.png .
 In this case the root directory points to the parent folder (which contains ’Plovdiv’ subfolder). This way you can have multiple subfolders containing different map tiles and all can be accessed through the same server!
 Access to local MBTiles files 
 … can be found on address: http://localhost:PORT/mbtiles – where PORT is set in application settings. In settings, you must specify a directory, where the files are stored. This directory is used as a root for the server. All files in that directory (including subdirectories) will be accessible from the server.
 As MBTiles use TMS schema to store map tiles, y coordinate must be transformed in order to locate the correct tile row. If your app uses XYZ tile schema, pass negative value for y (-y) as a parameter.
 There are several parameters, which must be provided:
 ’file’: MBTiles file (including extension)
 ’z’: map zoom level
 ’x’: x coordinate of a map tile
 ’y’: y coordinate of a map tile
 Example: If you have tiles stored in MBTiles format, you can place your files in the root directory and access them with: http://localhost:PORT/mbtiles/?tileset=test.mbtiles&z={z}&x={x}&y={y} or if XYZ schema is used: http://localhost:PORT/mbtiles/?tileset=test.mbtiles&z={z}&x={x}&y=-{y} 
 Redirect to a Tile Server with QuadKey Tile schema 
 Redirect can be accessed on address: http://localhost:PORT/redirect/?url=&quadkey=true&z=&x=&y= – where PORT is set in application settings. In settings, you must specify a directory, where the files are stored. This directory is used as a root for the server. All files in that directory (including subdirectories) will be accessible from the server.
 There are several parameters, which must be provided:
 ’url’: url address on which to redirect
 ’quadkey’: ’true’ if the server uses QuadKey Tile schema
 ’z’: map zoom level
 ’x’: x coordinate of a map tile
 ’y’: y coordinate of a map tile
 Example: If you want to use for example Bing Maps, which uses QuadKey Tile schema and you only have XYZ tile coordinates you can use the redirect option, which will calculate the quadkey value and then will redirect the request to the server. For accessing Bing Maps Aerial map tiles you can navigate to: http://localhost:PORT/redirect/?url=http://ecn.t0.tiles.virtualearth.net/tiles/a{quadkey}.jpeg?g=6201&quadkey=true&z={z}&x={x}&y={y}

izzyondroid:com.rendox.routinetracker.name: Routine Tracker
izzyondroid:com.rendox.routinetracker.summary: planner calendar app and a habit tracker
izzyondroid:com.rendox.routinetracker.description:
Routine Tracker is a planner that aims to simplify managing activities that you need to perform consistently. It combines features of a planner calendar app and a habit tracker allowing you to keep all your activities in one place.
 Features: 
 Flexible schedules: The app supports daily, weekly, monthly, and alternate-day schedules. You're free to choose specific days or inform the app how many times you wish to complete the task within a period.
 Adaptive schedule that changes automatically based on your progress: When you fail to complete your routine, you’ll be suggested to sort out the backlog on the next non-due day. And vice versa, when you over-complete your routine, the next scheduled occurrence will be canceled. This behavior can be altered in the settings.
 Adequate streaks: Streaks do not only form out of multiple completions in a row. Non-due days are included in the streak as well. Your streak will remain unbroken as long as you complete the habit the planned number of times within a given period.
 Plan ahead: The routine calendar displays completions, streaks, and planning dates to help you visualize your progress and plan your future time effectively. View a clean and organized agenda for any date, eliminating visual clutter.
 Modern UI: Enjoy a visually appealing and modern interface, following the principles of the Material You design. The application supports both light and dark modes, landscape orientation, and dynamic color on Android versions 12 and later.
 Completely free app with no limitations: Track as many habits as you wish. Routine Tracker is entirely free and contains no ads or in-app purchases.
 Works offline and respects your privacy: Routine Tracker operates independently without needing an internet connection or online account registration. Your confidential data always remains on your device. Neither the developers nor any third parties can access your information.
 More to come, so stay tuned…

fdroid:app.pagedrop.description:
PageDrop is a phone-first companion for jailbroken Kindles running KOReader. Find a book, convert it if needed, and send it to your Kindle over Wi-Fi, all from one app.
Requires a jailbroken Kindle with KOReader and its SSH server enabled. The in-app "Get your Kindle ready" walkthrough explains each step.
Features:
- Find books in-app across public-domain and open libraries (Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, Internet Archive, Wikisource and more) and your own OPDS catalogs
- Add books from your phone, or capture downloads from websites inside PageDrop
- Converts EPUB, PDF and text to MOBI, with PDF reflow for text PDFs (scanned PDFs are not OCRed)
- Automatic book details: titles, authors and covers
- Send to the Kindle over SSH/SFTP and refresh its library
- Kindle tab: see what is on the Kindle and manage those books
- Conversion server: books that need converting are uploaded to PageDrop's server (it asks first) and deleted about 24 hours later. The server's code is in the repository, so you can run your own. One switch in Settings keeps everything on the phone, and if the server fails the phone converts instead
- Free and open source (GPL-3.0)
PageDrop does not host or provide books. Some book sources and websites may offer material that is not freely licensed; you are responsible for respecting copyright law in your country.
No account, no analytics, no ads. Which hosts PageDrop contacts: https://github.com/spandan-kumar/PageDrop/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md
Not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon.

fdroid:app.palimpsest.name: Palimpsest
fdroid:app.palimpsest.summary: Encrypted notes, diary and to-dos with hidden vaults behind one password
fdroid:app.palimpsest.description:
Palimpsest is an encrypted diary and notes app with deniable vaults : one password field, any number of vaults, and no way to tell from the file how many there are. Every password opens its own vault. A decoy password shows a believable diary; another shows the real one.
 Experimental, not audited. It protects against a curious partner, a thief and a quick border check. It does not protect against a forensic lab, spyware on the phone, or someone who keeps demanding passwords. If an adversary keeps copies of the file from different moments and knows a decoy password, a hidden vault can give itself away. The threat model in the source repository has the details.
 Writing 
 Notes in a grid with folders, tags, pins and colours; a diary with a timeline and a month calendar; to-dos
 Markdown editor that hides the markers away from the line you edit
 Photos and voice notes captured in memory, never in the gallery; photos cropped before they are stored, EXIF and location dropped
 Links between entries, backlinks and a graph of links where you link entries by dragging one onto another
 Search, search inside an entry, trash with 30-day expiry
 Vaults 
 Create, change the password, delete a vault (its blocks are overwritten in place)
 A one-shot rule: on the next opening of this vault, destroy the vault with password X
 Backup of everything, restore, export of one vault under its own password, import with merging
 Privacy 
 No internet permission, no trackers, no ads
 Screenshots blocked unless you allow them; no preview in recent apps
 Incognito keyboard, no autofill, copied text cleared after 60 seconds
 Locks on screen off, after idle time and in the background
 The core is written in Rust: Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305 and BLAKE2b; the container is a pile of 4096-byte blocks that all look like random bytes, with random chaff added all the time.

fdroid:com.awakeonlanmobile.description:
AwakeOnLANMobile enables you to send Wake On LAN ( WOL ) packets, allowing you to remotely wake up your devices over either a local area network (LAN) or over the internet. It supports IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. The application offers several features:
 Open Source : Licensed under GPLv3 License with zero advertisements and no account creation necessary.
 Local Storage : Add, edit, or delete device information for easy access.
 Network Scanning : Discover devices using either an IPv4 address or CIDR notation for subnets (e.g., 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.1.1/24). Choose between PING and TCP connect (sent to Port 443) packets for scanning. PING will require 1 second per IP address, while TCP connect will be faster.
 Theme Toggle : Switch between a light and dark mode theme to customize the appearance based on your preferences. The selected theme will be persisted even after shutting down the application.
 Developed with React Native (Typescript) and utilizes C++ turbo modules for native level socket access when sending and receiving packets. The ./cpp directory contains lightly modified code from 'https://github.com/nellogan/awakeonlan' and 'https://github.com/nellogan/netscan'. These are Linux commandline utilities that can be used in lieu of this application if your device supports a terminal (such as Termux or the new Android AVF Linux terminal).

fdroid:com.demosten.srednabg.name: SrednaBG
fdroid:com.demosten.srednabg.summary: Real-time average speed inside Bulgaria's average-speed camera zones.
fdroid:com.demosten.srednabg.description:
SrednaBG shows your real-time running average speed inside Bulgaria's average-speed camera zones — and tells you the maximum speed you can sustain for the rest of the zone without going over the limit.
Free. Open source. Bulgaria only.
WHAT IT DOES
• Running average, live — The moment you enter a zone, your running average becomes the hero number. No lag, no jitter. Updates every second.
• Max now — Shows the top speed you can drive for the rest of the zone without breaking the limit. Waze tells you the zone exists; SrednaBG tells you what to do about it.
• Green / amber / red at a glance — The screen color tracks your state. Green: within limit. Amber: careful, slow down. Red: already over.
• Voice alerts in Bulgarian and English — Keep your eyes on the road. SrednaBG speaks zone entries, exits, and slowdown warnings in the language you choose.
• Works fully offline — The Bulgaria map and zone list are bundled inside the app. No internet needed in the car. Updates arrive quietly when you're on Wi-Fi.
• Alongside Waze, or instead of it — Run SrednaBG as a full navigator, or let it sit quietly behind Waze / Google Maps — you'll hear its voice when it matters.
PERMISSIONS, EXPLAINED
• Background location — Average-speed zones can be many kilometres long, and a drive often outlasts the screen timeout or runs behind another navigation app. SrednaBG needs location while in the background so your average keeps updating with the screen off or another app in front. It is used only to compute your speed inside zones — never shared, and it never leaves your phone.
• Ignore battery optimizations (optional) — You can grant an exemption so the system doesn't suspend tracking mid-drive. It is optional and requested only from a card you tap; tracking still starts without it, just less reliably on devices with aggressive power management.
PRIVACY
• No cookies, no trackers anywhere.
• No account, no email, no signup. Install and drive.
• No ads. No in-app purchases. Free forever.
• No third-party SDKs. No Google Analytics. No Firebase.
• Your location never leaves your phone.
Open source — MIT License.
Source code: https://github.com/demosten-com/SrednaBG

fdroid:com.health.openscale.sync.name: openScale sync
fdroid:com.health.openscale.sync.summary: Synchronize your openScale measurements with external services
fdroid:com.health.openscale.sync.description:
Synchronize your openScale measurements with external services
openScale sync is a companion app: it requires the separate openScale app (a bluetooth body-composition scale app) to be installed. It stores no measurements of its own. It reads them from openScale and forwards them to the services you enable, and it can bring measurements the other way as well, back into openScale.
Features:
* Seamless External Service Integration: Effortlessly synchronize data with Health Connect, Wger, Endurain, SparkyFitness, InfluxDB, generic Webhooks and MQTT (versions 3.1 and 5.0, including Home Assistant discovery).
* Real-time Synchronization: Automatically synchronize data upon insertion, editing, deletion, or clearing of measurements within openScale.
* Two-way Synchronization: Measurements that other apps wrote to Health Connect, Wger or MQTT can be imported back into openScale, filling the gaps your scale did not record. Each service has its own direction setting: export only, import only, or both.
* Optional Background Synchronization: Let the app reconcile everything every few hours, as a safety net for when the instant sync could not run.
* On-Demand Full Synchronization: Initiate a complete data synchronization manually whenever needed.
* Automatic Retry: A sync that could not be delivered is retried on its own with the current data, and any measurement still waiting is shown to you.
* Multi-User Aware: MQTT, InfluxDB and Webhook keep every openScale user separate; Health Connect, Wger, Endurain and SparkyFitness sync the user you select.
* Configurable Service Activation: Easily enable or disable individual external services to tailor your synchronization preferences.
* Intelligent Foreground Service: Utilizes a foreground service that activates only when required, minimizing battery consumption.
* Intuitive User Interface: Enjoy a user-friendly graphical interface for effortless navigation and control.
Your data is never sent anywhere except the services you enable and configure yourself. The app has no ads, no analytics and no accounts.

fdroid:com.raulshma.lenscast.name: LensCast
fdroid:com.raulshma.lenscast.summary: Turn your phone into a networked camera: web, MJPEG and RTSP streaming
fdroid:com.raulshma.lenscast.description:
LensCast turns your Android device into a networked camera station with professional controls, remote web access, interval photography, and scheduled recording.
Camera
• Live preview with a professional quick settings bar
• Manual controls: exposure compensation, ISO, white balance, focus mode, zoom
• Multi-lens support (ultra-wide, wide, telephoto) with runtime lens switching
• HDR, image stabilization, resolution up to 4K, frame rate 15–60 fps
• Photo capture and video recording
• Night vision / IR mode, scene modes, manual focus distance, color temperature
Live streaming
• Real-time MJPEG video streaming to any web browser on the same network
• Low-latency in-browser playback (WebCodecs over WebSocket) with automatic fallback to MJPEG and HLS
• RTSP streaming with AAC audio and H.264/H.265 video at 480p/720p/1080p for VLC, OBS, and NVRs
• ONVIF Profile S device service (off by default) so NVRs such as Home Assistant can discover the camera
• HTTPS mode with a self-signed on-device certificate
Web dashboard
• Watch the live stream, browse and download photos and recordings
• Full remote control of camera and stream settings
• Optional password authentication
Automation
• Object detection gate (optional): the open-source EfficientDet-Lite0 model — Apache-2.0, downloaded on demand with a pinned SHA-256 from TensorFlow's official hosting — triggers MQTT alerts or recording when configured objects appear
• Sound-event gate (optional): the open-source YAMNet model — Apache-2.0, also downloaded on demand with a pinned SHA-256 — triggers alerts or recording when configured sounds are detected
• Interval photography and scheduled or continuous recording
• Quiet hours for notifications
Optional network services (all off by default; each runs only when you enable and configure it)
• Telegram backup: auto-uploads new captures to the Telegram chat you choose (api.telegram.org)
• Web Push notifications: delivers encrypted detection alerts through your browser vendor's push service (such as Google's FCM or Mozilla's autopush)
• Model downloads: the optional detection models above are fetched on demand from TensorFlow's official hosting on Google Cloud storage
• STUN server for WebRTC streaming (WHIP push / WHEP viewing): blank by default, so streaming stays on your local network without contacting any third-party server
No ads, no tracking, no cloud defaults. All processing stays on your device; the web dashboard is served by a built-in HTTP server on your local network.
Note: the F-Droid build ships without the in-app self-updater; updates come from F-Droid.

Each pair decides: a full copy; titles and locations only; or "Busy" blocks that show your time and nothing else. Put a label in front of copied titles — "[Work] Standup", or "[Work] Busy" — and carry the meeting link into the copy's notes so a mirrored meeting is one you can join.
CHOOSE WHICH EVENTS

IT TELLS YOU WHEN SOMETHING BREAKS
A healthy pair is silent. If one stops syncing, an all-day warning appears in the destination calendar itself, and clears the moment the pair recovers.
ON IPHONE AND IPAD
Every pair in one list, with its health and event count. Pull down to sync now. Background refreshes run at the interval you choose, when iOS allows — treat it as the earliest a sync may start, not a guarantee.
SEND TIMES
"When are you free?" One tap gives you your next three free times as a line of text — "Tue 2–2:30pm, Wed 10–10:30am or Thu 3–3:30pm MDT" — worked out on your device from the calendars you chose, ready to paste into Messages, Mail or Slack. Also a Shortcuts action and a Siri phrase. Nothing leaves your device.
ASKWHEN.ME — A SEPARATE PRODUCT YOU CAN TURN ON
Off by default; until you turn it on, the app makes no network request of any kind. AskWhen.me is a subscription with its own server: a page at askwhen.me/yourpage where people can ask you for a time.
A request page, not a booking page. Your device works out which times to offer and sends only those — never your calendar, your events, your address, or your name beyond the label you choose. Someone picks a time and says who they are; the request comes to your device, and nothing lands in your calendar until you accept. Your device re-checks the time against your real calendar first.
Send times can carry a personal link: it opens your page once, for a week, and because you sent it there is no email confirmation — if the time is still clear, your device accepts it for you and they get the calendar file.
Free for 90 days, then $19.99 a year; your own name on askwhen.me, or your own domain, are upgrades. Payment is Apple's. The privacy page says what the server holds, and for how long.

• No unified calendar view — it makes copies; your calendar app shows them.
• No team, admin or SSO features. It is a single-person utility.
• Attendees are never copied: Apple's calendar framework cannot set guests.
• It cannot sync a calendar your device cannot already see.
PRIVACY
No account. No analytics, no tracking, no telemetry, no ads. No server, and no network request, until you turn on AskWhen.me — and its server never sees your calendar either. Once a copy lands in iCloud, Google or Exchange, that provider stores it under their policies.

debian-packages:backup2l.description:
backup2l [backup-too-l] is a tool for autonomously generating, maintaining
and restoring backups on a mountable file system (e. g. hard disk). In a
default installation, backups are created regularly by a cron script.
The main design goals are low maintenance effort, efficiency, transparency
and robustness. All control files are stored together with the archives on
the backup device, and their contents are mostly self-explaining. Hence, a
user can - if necessary - browse the files and extract archives manually.
backup2l features differential backups at multiple hierarchical levels.
This allows one to generate small incremental backups at short intervals
while at the same time, the total number of archives only increases
logarithmically with the number of backups since the last full backup.
An open driver architecture allows one to use virtually any archiving
program as a backend. Built-in drivers support .tar.gz, .tar.bz2 and others.
Further user-defined drivers can be added.
An integrated split-and-collect function allows one to comfortably transfer
all or selected archives to a set of CDs or other removable media.

flathub:org.archivekeep.ArchiveKeep.name: ArchiveKeep
flathub:org.archivekeep.ArchiveKeep.description:
ArchiveKeep helps you preserve your personal files by maintaining identical copies across multiple
 storage locations — without risking corruption or data loss during synchronization.
 Once a file is archived, it stays unchanged. ArchiveKeep never overwrites existing copies with
 modifications or corrupted data, ensuring your archives remain intact over time.
 Features:
 Plain files — no proprietary format, readable with any application.
 Incremental synchronization — replicates new files or moves when storages become available,
 working fully offline.
 SHA-256 file fingerprinting — fast verification that catches silent bit-rot before it spreads.
 Multi-platform — available on Linux desktop and Android.
 No vendor lock-in — you control where your files live.
 Supported cloud storages:
 Google Drive — convenient, familiar, widely available.
 S3-compatible APIs — choose any vendor that supports the S3 protocol.
 ArchiveKeep is in active development and improving with each release. Feedback and bug reports
 are welcome.

fedora-packages:argon2/argon2.name: argon2
fedora-packages:argon2/argon2.description: Argon2 is a password-hashing function that summarizes the state of the art in the design of memory-hard functions and can be used to hash passwords for credential storage, key derivation, or other applications. It has a simple design aimed at the highest memory filling rate and effective use of multiple computing units, while still providing defense against tradeoff attacks (by exploiting the cache and memory organization of the recent processors). Argon2 has three variants: Argon2i, Argon2d, and Argon2id. * Argon2d is faster and uses data-depending memory access, which makes it highly resistant against GPU cracking attacks and suitable for applications with no threats from side-channel timing attacks (eg. cryptocurrencies). * Argon2i instead uses data-independent memory access, which is preferred for password hashing and password-based key derivation, but it is slower as it makes more passes over the memory to protect from tradeoff attacks. * Argon2id is a hybrid of Argon2i and Argon2d, using a combination of data-depending and data-independent memory accesses, which gives some of Argon2i's resistance to side-channel cache timing attacks and much of Argon2d's resistance to GPU cracking attacks.

fedora-packages:ax86-terminus-ttf-fonts/.description: Terminus TTF is a TrueType version of Terminus Font, a fixed-width bitmap font optimized for long work with computers. If the application you want to use the font with supports the original Terminus Font, you should really use that one instead of this TTF version — it will most likely be a more pleasant experience for you. There are applications that neither support the original Terminus Font nor use bitmaps embedded in TrueType fonts. They completely rely on the automatically generated scalable outlines. When Terminus TTF is used with such applications, it will probably look a little bit weird and not exactly like the original Terminus Font (since the generated outlines do not exactly match the bitmaps); you will see whether you like it or not. Because the outlines are scalable, it should not matter which size you use, but anything bigger than 32 px (24 pt) will probably not look very nice. It should also be noted that you need to render Terminus TTF in monochrome black/white if the outlines are used; otherwise, they will look smeary.

 Firefox Sync Account (recommended)
 EverSync
 Session Sync will automatically detect new updates and display the updated sessions list across multiple machines.
General features
 - active session management (move around tabs)
 - advanced bookmark management
 - session restore with lazy-loading
 - session auto-saving (not backed by Bookmarks)
 - history list - session can be saved later as classic bookmark sessions
 - private windows are ignored by auto-save
 - auto-saving is only intended as a nice addition and is not full-featured (please look for other addons for complete auto-saving support) 
 - session filtering (search text) and sorting by name/position/date
 - advanced drag-n-drop UI with fluid animations
 - advance UI scaling for individual UI areas (session list, bookmark list, session header and toolbar)
 - 3 working modes: Panel, Tab View, Window View
 - many other customization
 Required permission explained: 
 Read and modify bookmarks - required for storing sessions as bookmarks as well as interacting with them
 Input data to the clipboard - required for right-click menu in order to copy bookmark title/URL
 Access browser tabs - required in order to be able to read/save browsing session information. (This provides only tab properties and not actual browsing content)
 Store unlimited amount of client-side data - Required for addon Settings, favicon caching, auto-saved history as well as additional information for sessions
 All data is stored local and/or is synced on your Firefox Account (bookmarks).

apple-macos:6825368673.description:
Finances shows you at a glance how much money you have left this month – and what that means per day.
HOW IT WORKS
• Set a monthly budget and see what’s left
• Your month starts when you want – on payday, for example
• Log expenses in seconds: type the amount, pick a category, done
• Category suggestions by merchant – sort it once and the app remembers
• Choose your currency: €, $, £, CHF and more
FIXED COSTS IN ONE PLACE
• Rent, insurance, phone, subscriptions and one-time payments at a glance
• Shared costs: add who pays how much
• Reminders before every payment and a weekly preview
• See what’s left after fixed costs and what can go to savings
INSIGHTS & SAVINGS GOALS
• Monthly trend compared with last month
• Spending by category and category budgets
• Savings goals with an expected date
LOG WALLET PAYMENTS AUTOMATICALLY
With a Shortcuts automation, card payments from Wallet land in the app by themselves. You only confirm the category – right from the notification.
IPHONE AND MAC
Your data syncs through your private iCloud. Widgets for the Home Screen, Lock Screen and Mac desktop.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your data stays on your devices and in your own iCloud. Optional lock with Face ID or Touch ID.

apple-itunes:6760258084.name: Uni:Note – Study Notes
apple-itunes:6760258084.description:
Create problem sets and study with “Learned” and “Not Yet”, all within your note app. With Uni:Note, you can review alongside your original notes and study problem sets in the companion app Uni:Note Pocket by importing a backup.
Uni:Note is a handwriting app for iPad with a simple, ad-free interface that lets you write as you would in a paper notebook.
Designed under the guidance of a current university student, it focuses on being easy to use in class.
Along with Apple Pencil handwriting, it supports writing on images and PDFs, vertical notebooks, and multiple windows.
Keep taking notes while working with class handouts and PDF materials.
Use the notes you write for review.
Study Assistant (AI) supports Circle to Solve, problem set generation, and AI Summary. You can also create and edit problem sets yourself.
Recording and real-time transcription are also supported.
Take notes while recording a class, then use AI Summary to summarize the transcription.
Customize the navigation bar and palette to suit the tools you use most.
■Key Features
• Create and edit problem sets with handwriting, the keyboard, pasted text, or TSV/CSV files
• AI problem set generation from your notes
• Study with “Learned” and “Not Yet”, resume where you left off, and shuffle questions
• Review with your original notes displayed alongside
• Study problem sets imported from a backup in Uni:Note Pocket
• Handwriting with Apple Pencil
• Writing on images and PDFs
• Vertical notebooks and multiple windows
• Recording and real-time transcription
• AI Summary and Circle to Solve
• Sticky Marker
• Ruler, Move Selection
• Undo and Redo for moves and changes to shapes, pasted images and PDFs, and sticky notes, plus lines drawn with the ruler
• Open the Button Guide with “?” (from the “…” menu in a notebook)
• Pomodoro timer
• Navigation bar and palette customization
• Export PDF
• Backup and restore
■About Privacy
Uni:Note uses in-app identifiers that do not directly identify you to manage your AI Balance and purchase status.
It also collects diagnostic information, such as crash logs when the app crashes, to investigate issues.
When you use AI features, data needed for processing, such as selected note content and transcriptions, is sent to an AI service to generate answers, problem sets, summaries, and similar output.
Routine diagnostic information does not include information that directly identifies you or the contents of notes, audio, transcriptions, or attachments.
The information collected is used to provide AI features, manage their use, and improve app quality.

apple-macos:6760626211.name: PommeCore
apple-macos:6760626211.description:
PommeCore is the full-featured companion app for MeshCore LoRa mesh radios — a decentralized, off-grid messaging network that works without internet, cell towers, or servers. Everything runs over long-range LoRa radio, directly between devices.
MESSAGING
Send and receive direct messages with real-time delivery tracking (Sending → Sent → Delivered, with round-trip time). Channel (group) messages broadcast to everyone on the mesh. Reactions and quoted replies are interoperable with MeshCore One. Undelivered messages retry automatically, then flood the mesh.
CONTACTS & CHANNELS
Organise contacts with favourites, nicknames, notes, and groups. Mute or block individuals. Each group and channel has its own notification mode and sound. Export and import contacts via QR code or meshcore:// URLs.
MESH MAP
See all contacts with GPS on an interactive map. Tap a pin to open that contact's chat. Enable position trails for movement history. The link quality overlay draws colour-coded lines (SNR) to contacts in range.
RADIO SETTINGS & TOOLS
Configure frequency, spreading factor, bandwidth, coding rate, and TX power from the app. Radio Stats, RF Monitor with Packet Log, Line of Sight analysis, Radio Calculator, Airtime Calculator, and Frequency Scanner are all included.
BACKUP & UPDATES
Export your radio configuration as a .meshprofile file. Firmware update checker alerts you when a new release is available. Over-the-air ESP32 firmware updates via WiFi.
REMOTE MANAGEMENT
Administer repeaters and room servers over the mesh — change names, frequencies, routing scope, and advert intervals without physical access.
WIDGETS & WATCH
Home screen and lock screen widgets show connection status, battery, and unread count. The watchOS companion lets you read and reply to DMs and channel messages from your wrist.
iPHONE, iPAD & MAC
One app runs natively on iPhone, iPad, and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel). Connects via Bluetooth LE, WiFi, or USB serial on Mac.
LANGUAGES
English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Czech, Polish, Ukrainian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese.
ACCESSIBILITY
VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, Differentiate Without Color Alone, Dark Mode, Voice Control.
PRIVACY
No account required. No servers. No data collection. All communication is peer-to-peer over LoRa radio. iCloud sync for nicknames, notes, groups, and settings uses your private iCloud account.
HARDWARE REQUIRED
A MeshCore-compatible LoRa radio running Companion firmware is required. Recommended: Compatible Mesh radio with latest MeshCore Companion firmware
IN-APP PURCHASES
Tip Jar ($0.99–$9.99) — voluntary support, no functional gating.
PommeCore for Apple Watch ($1.99, one-time) — unlocks the watch companion app.
All other features are free.
